guarantees neither convergence nor the adequacy of those conditions, and

This member owns the product-definition-routing bounded context,
`urn:stdo:bounded-context:product-definition-routing`, under the selected
complete STDO basis, and defines that context's overlay, definition,
discovery, locator and composition concepts. The JSON schema named below
realises the accepted interoperability shape of the overlay and is not a
second semantic owner

Product-Definition Identity is product.definition_id, a URI identifying the mutable continuing WHAT-definition line, unique in the discovered workspace definition set, distinct from immutable Product and release identities.

grounding.quote:
The suffix `<label>` is the Definition Label: a stable lowercase local
discovery label of ASCII letters, digits, hyphens or underscores, unique
only among the definitions in the same directory. It is not Product
identity. The `product.definition_id` URI inside the definition is the

product-definition line, unique within the discovered workspace definition
set. It identifies one continuing WHAT definition, not one immutable
released Product (P3).

Its ten rows distinguish consequences, owners of added domain/interoperability/policy choices, rule loci, pillars and consumers; it does not own the imported FOUNDATIONS rule.

The index also assigns to this family the rule of
[FOUNDATIONS §2 Imports between members](FOUNDATIONS.md#imports-between-members);

concepts.label: F12 foundation-to-law family

concepts.definition: Complete selected governing-document set for a product, with no prescribed file count, collectively making recoverable axioms (starting truths, invariants, refusals), ontology (kinds, identities, relations, boundaries, lifecycle), epistemology (evidence, observation, uncertainty, falsification, decision authority), taxonomy (classifications preventing category collapse) and semantics (terms, relations, states, operations, outcomes).

grounding.quote:
A Constitutional Set is the complete set of governing documents selected
for a product, not a prescribed number of files. Collectively the selected
set makes five things recoverable for the governed scope (P2, P1; rc.2
#constitutional-set-sufficiency):

concepts.label: Constitutional Set

concepts.definition: Pair of immutable stdo://releases/<cut>/ URI and installed-manifest SHA-256. The URI identifies an immutable annotated RC cut; the deterministic manifest binds tag object, commit, repository tree, standards subtree, exact standards inventory, member bytes and admitted auxiliary payloads. Its schema is schemas/installed-release-manifest.schema.json; it is transport/integrity evidence, not a replacement constitution.

grounding.quote:
The URI identifies one immutable annotated RC cut. The digest identifies
the deterministic installed-release manifest, which binds the cut's tag
object, commit, repository tree, standards subtree, exact standards
inventory, member bytes and admitted auxiliary payloads. The manifest shape
is owned by `schemas/installed-release-manifest.schema.json`. The manifest
is transport and integrity evidence, not a replacement constitution (P6).

concepts.label: Installed Release Basis

concepts.definition: Read-only deterministic acceptance object binding current Product Definition identity/bytes/current basis to a resolved immutable target cut, annotated tag object, commit, tree and installed-manifest digest. Its SHA-256 is an operator-presentable acceptance token, not authority by possession. A Fleet Adoption Plan binds an authorised fleet root and complete ordered per-definition plan-digest set.

grounding.quote:
An Adoption Plan is the read-only, deterministic acceptance object that
binds one current Product Definition's identity and bytes to its current
basis and to one resolved immutable target's cut, annotated tag object,
commit, tree and installed-manifest digest. Its SHA-256 is the
operator-presentable acceptance token. Possession of the token alone grants
no authority; a mismatch proves that the presented subject is no longer the
subject being mutated (P6, P3). A Fleet Adoption Plan binds an authorised
fleet root and the complete ordered set of per-definition plan digests
under the same law.

concepts.label: Adoption Plan and Fleet Adoption Plan

concepts.definition: Bounded executable realisation installing each immutable cut once in a shared versioned store, resolving logical release URIs to verified bytes, inventorying/verifying complete distributions, synchronising selected exact bases, producing digest-bound adoption plans and adopting only accepted plans, managing marker-bounded declared agent-file bootstrap, and applying these operations to explicitly discovered fleets.
concepts.label: STDO Toolchain Manager

grounding.quote:
An ODD product is built correctly only when every clause of this section
holds (P6).

constraints.statement: Holding every clause of §11 is necessary for an ODD product to be built correctly; this only-when condition does not independently assert sufficiency or actual correctness.

grounding.quote:
The product works over explicit typed assets or typed nodes. It does not
work over one hidden project blob, one giant mutable workspace object or one
undocumented service payload. Concrete assets must bind explicitly into
typed domain boundaries. Where an asset is a real produced or consumed boundary,
its `asset_surface` is declared (P3).

constraints.statement: The product must work over explicit typed assets/nodes, not a hidden project blob, giant mutable workspace object or undocumented service payload. Every concrete asset binds explicitly into a typed domain boundary; an asset_surface is declared wherever the asset is a real produced or consumed boundary.

grounding.quote:
Every operative constructive step is carried by one named `GraphFunction`
or one lawful graph-function composition. The real carrier is never left
inside orchestration loops, bespoke Python pipeline runners, controller
scripts, or service methods that only happen to call GTL-adjacent helpers
(P0, P4a).

constraints.statement: Every operative constructive step has one named GraphFunction or one lawful composition as its carrier. Orchestration loops, bespoke Python pipeline runners, controller scripts and service methods merely calling GTL-adjacent helpers cannot hide the real carrier.
constraints.uncertainty: The complete law defining lawful composition is not supplied.

conditions: Construction of the product's own operative framework behaviour.

grounding.quote:
Because this profile makes an edge traversal the unit of compute, an ODD
product must use that unit of compute to build its own operative framework
behaviour. The required order is: declare the outcome
traversal over typed assets; publish the declarative GTL/ABG carrier
structure; implement only the minimal imperative adapter code that remains
necessary (P0, P6).

constraints.statement: Use edge traversal as the unit of compute to build operative framework behaviour, in order: declare the outcome traversal over typed assets; publish declarative GTL/ABG structure; implement only remaining necessary minimal imperative adapters. Imperative-first behaviour later described in GTL vocabulary is ODD-shaped but not yet ODD-built.

grounding.quote:
The live line must publish a machine-readable function catalogue. At
minimum each retained function should expose its name, inputs, outputs,
intent, and public or helper role. A callable surface that exists only in
prose or in prompt memory leaves the product under-built (P6, P3).

constraints.statement: The live line must publish a machine-readable catalogue. At minimum every retained function should expose name, inputs, outputs, intent and public/helper role; this field guidance remains 'should'. A callable surface existing only in prose or prompt memory leaves the product under-built.

grounding.quote:
Where a public carrier refines into inner executable structure, the live
traversal boundaries are published explicitly through lawful GTL boundary
surfaces such as `RefinementBoundary` or `CandidateFamily`. The outer
public carrier remains the callable contract (P4a, P3).

constraints.statement: Publish public graph-function carriers, their graph(s), typed node/vector surfaces and semantic jobs or equivalent bound outer callable contracts. Never bind callers directly to hidden inner vectors. If the public carrier refines into executable inner structure, explicitly publish live traversal boundaries through lawful surfaces such as RefinementBoundary or CandidateFamily; the outer carrier remains the callable contract.
constraints.uncertainty: The examples name boundary surfaces without supplying their complete definitions.

conditions: ODD application over GTL/ABG.

grounding.quote:
The product may publish typed assets and evidence, execute one admitted
bounded constructive step, publish downstream read models or domain
overlays, and return control to ABG. The product must not own a hidden
continuation loop; carry multi-step controller memory across publish
boundaries; infer later steps locally instead of re-entering through ABG;
treat public `next` and explicit graph-function continuation as rival
authorities inside one controller; or build product-local orchestration
that in effect replaces ABG (P6).

constraints.statement: The application is a cooperative subsystem, not a replacement runtime. ABG owns continuation, re-entry after publication, graph-call lifecycle and declared-graph step selection. Product permission is bounded to publishing typed assets/evidence, executing one admitted step, publishing downstream read models/overlays and returning control. Hidden continuation loops, multi-step memory across publish boundaries, local inference of later steps, rival public-next/explicit-continuation authorities and replacement product orchestration are prohibited. Tenant-local replacement of ABG continuation constitutes a different architecture despite ODD-shaped artifacts.

conditions: Changes to runtime, start/iterate, worker transport, actor invocation, process supervision, plugin dispatch, event projection, closure, assurance, retry or continuation semantics.
exceptions: A different runtime realisation is lawful only with an explicitly ratified, non-overlapping runtime scope.

grounding.quote:
The audit must prove that exactly one execution authority exists for the
affected traversal. For a consumer using the GTL and ABG roles, that
authority is the one consumer-bound realisation of the ABG role, including
when the realisation under change itself implements that role. A
different realisation is lawful only under an explicitly ratified,
non-overlapping runtime scope (P6, P3).

constraints.statement: Before activation and closure, prove exactly one execution authority for the affected traversal: the consumer-bound ABG realisation, including when that realisation is under change. Inventory at least: traversal selection/vector advance—ABG, with product graph/vector/asset/policy declarations and no local next-step runner; actor invocation/supervision—ABG, with actor bindings/prompts/payload/evidence adapters and no spawn/spawnSync/exec/timeout/kill/stdout/stderr supervision outside its actor seam; retry/correction/continuation/re-entry—ABG, with bounded outputs/control return and no local retry loops, carried controller memory or hidden next; runtime emission/append/replay/projection—ABG, with admitted domain payload mapping and no bypassing event append, ledger mutation or projection reconstruction; closure fold/assurance gate—ABG with product policy/gain inputs, domain interpretation/evaluators/gap reasons/weights, and no worker self-report or product postflight directly closing runtime units. Artifact review alone is insufficient: include language/tenant-appropriate code, call-graph or static-surface review and name evidence excluding hidden authority.

conditions: Any listed forbidden condition is present.

grounding.quote:
When any is present, the product may be useful but is not currently
ODD-correct over GTL/ABG (P6).

constraints.statement: Each independently prevents closure and current ODD correctness: downstream start/iterate loop for an ABG traversal; product/plugin worker supervision outside the actor seam; retry/continuation/re-entry state outside ABG; runtime-event append or ledger mutation without ABG admission; plugin output carrying next-vector, closure, actor-invocation, process or runtime-event authority rather than evidence/policy input; two controllers each able to claim one traversal. Usefulness does not remove this refusal.

conditions: Audited surfaces admit a consequential entity transformation.

grounding.quote:
ABG's broader execution, supervision, retry and projection authority
continues to derive from this profile and is not thereby reclassified as
admission authority. `F_P` and `F_H` are the ODD projections of the
candidate-producer and human-adjudication roles, which this profile binds
to the source concepts of SPEC_METHOD §5 in
[§5 Probabilistic compute](#probabilistic-compute) (P6, P1).

constraints.statement: ABG transformation-admission authority is a graph-native specialisation of admission completeness owned by ACTIVATION §4, with predecessor restatement in DESIGN_MODULE and rc.2 STDO-UP-016 as provenance. Broader execution, supervision, retry and projection authority remains ODD-profile authority and is not reclassified as admission. ODD F_P/F_H project candidate-producer/human-adjudication roles through §5 bindings to SPEC_METHOD §5.
constraints.uncertainty: The owning admission semantics and role bindings are outside the supplied source.

grounding.quote:
Name equality is not enough. A same-named graph function, node, carrier,
policy or route with different inputs, outputs, vectors, declarations,
ownership or closure law is a different truth surface until reconciled.
Negative proof for a projection must include structural drift, not only
missing source truth (P3, P6).

constraints.statement: Read models may summarise/index/filter/render admitted carrier/runtime/event/source truth but cannot reconstruct parallel authority. Function-catalogue views reconcile to the admitted GTL module/public carrier; asset ownership/start-target views derive from or structurally compare with their admitted carrier; runtime status derives from ABG facts/events/replay/projection truth; domain overlays fail closed for missing, stale or structurally divergent carriers. Matching names do not reconcile differing inputs, outputs, vectors, declarations, ownership or closure law. Projection negative proof includes structural drift as well as missing source truth.

exceptions: Further material work after a terminal or exhausted basis requires another admitted basis.

grounding.quote:
The loop selects no further material work without another admitted basis
once the selected outcome is accepted; an admitted prerequisite is
discharged; an admitted experiment's stated decision is resolved; another
admitted terminal condition is reached; or its governing basis or bound
is exhausted, rejected, withdrawn, superseded, repriced away or
falsified. A `reprice` disposition requests lawful constitutional
re-entry; it neither performs the reprice nor selects the successor
outcome (P2, P6).

constraints.statement: The selected Product outcome is external authority: models, gaps, assurance, ledgers and projections may interpret but cannot author/select/enlarge it. evaluate_next selects material work only within that outcome or an admitted bounded prerequisite/experiment. Edge/graph closure is evidence toward, never itself, Product or release acceptance. Stop material selection without another admitted basis upon outcome acceptance, prerequisite discharge, experiment decision resolution, another admitted terminal condition, or exhausted/rejected/withdrawn/superseded/repriced-away/falsified governing basis or bound. Reprice requests constitutional re-entry; it neither reprices nor selects a successor outcome.
constraints.uncertainty: STDO-UP-013/SPEC_METHOD §3 is referenced but not supplied.

exceptions: Underlying libraries may be shared without sharing authority.

grounding.quote:
A module that lets one of these
functions exercise another's authority creates a rival control surface
and violates A0 (P6).

constraints.statement: synthesize_model(IntentLineage, prior ProductAssetModel, admitted product truth)→ProductAssetModel may update desired/known typed model truth only, and must not observe Worksite, admit intent, select/invoke/close work. eval_gap(ProductAssetModel, RuntimeEventLog, RuntimeProjection, Worksite)→ObservationSnapshot+GapPressureRow compares desired truth with reality read-only; it does not admit intent, select/invoke/close work. evaluate_next(NextActionBasis, fresh eval_gap, TargetObligationBinding, ActionCatalog, Policy)→PriorityProjection+NextActionProjection+selected_action, plus its own core result for typed no-action; it may bind obligations and rank/select only published lawful actions matching gap and governing basis, never admit intent or judge an earlier action except by consuming admitted EdgeClosureDecision. evaluate_action(ConstructionIntent, AdmittedEvidence, TargetObligationBinding, Policy)→EdgeFulfillmentLedger+EdgeClosureDecision folds admitted evidence to judge close/yield/retry/repair/re-enter/reprice/block for the action just taken, never selects the next action. Designs, tickets, code modules and proofs must name which function they implement/consume rather than merely say evaluator.

grounding.quote:
`ConstructionIntent` must cite the lineage, the
selected action and the `TargetObligationBinding` that preserve the exact
selected Product outcome and any admitted bounded-basis refs (P4b, P6).

constraints.statement: Bootstrap/external intent may originate with a human, imported source, prior product or intent engine and seeds the model; current construction intent is synthesized against model and observed gap, then admitted by a distinct step after published-action selection. Intent cannot invent unpublished actions. Every constructive action binds the current gap to exact target assets/obligations before invocation using selected outcome ref, optional admitted prerequisite/experiment ref, pressure, assets, required roles and evidence refs. A broad edge satisfies a specific gap only if its binding proves lawfulness for those exact assets. ConstructionIntent cites lineage, selected action and target binding preserving authority refs. The declared intent→model→observation→gap→binding→priority→intent→evidence→ledger→decision→next-projection chain is the sole authoritative computational surface; CLI branches, prompt prose, postflight strings, dossier action lists, queries, services and local summaries cannot become rival traversal truth.

grounding.quote:
Every closure-relevant F_P callout that does work needs ledger admission.
Evaluator work is not outside F_P merely because it reads ledgers: it is
F_P work over governed ledger state, and its result must be admitted into
the immutable ledger and event spine before it can affect closure, routing
or traversal. Corrections append or supersede ledger and event facts; they
do not rewrite the governed history of work (P4b, P6, P3).

constraints.statement: Filesystem, process output, screen logs, worker artifacts and product files are observations, becoming authority only through typed-evidence admission and ledger/decision fold. W is mutable workspace; L immutable governed work ledger; E immutable event/replay spine; Ev evaluator work over L. L records admitted callout basis, deltas, file refs, digests, execution evidence, touched obligations, claims, evaluator inputs/outputs and admission status, not a workspace copy. F_P acts in W; admission records L; E anchors/orders entries with predecessor refs; Ev evaluates a declared L snapshot, not ambient W; its F_P output is admitted back into L/E before affecting closure/routing/traversal; L/E constrain subsequent lawful action. W may change without truth, L may be true without covering W, and closure/evaluation can use W only through L. Every working closure-relevant F_P callout needs admission; corrections append/supersede rather than rewrite history. Ledger attention is a structural analogy, not transformer dependency: evaluators may use only admitted rows reachable through declared lineage, predecessor refs, target binding, policy and relevant event cursor; outside workspace facts, prose, archives, summaries and controller memory are excluded.

exceptions: A completed graph after a closed edge has an empty selection without refusal or selection determination.

grounding.quote:
On `post_reprice`, `evaluate_next` must return a typed no-action
disposition while constitutional re-entry stays unresolved. The reprice
decision cannot authorise a replacement action; work may be evaluated
again only after lawful re-entry separately admits an exact selected
Product outcome or bounded basis and supplies it through a new
`initial_selection` or a basis-bearing resume. Default graph following is
ordinary, but it is still an `evaluate_next` decision and not hidden
sequential control (P5, P2, P6).

constraints.statement: evaluate_next is total and ranks only published lawful catalogue actions; unpublished desired actions yield typed no-action, never fallback executive graphs/local scripts. initial_selection uses current model/gap/binding/catalogue/policy. post_yield_resume resumes or yields the same edge from replay-visible truth without failure classification. post_close_graph_continuation may select the next edge or none if complete. For post_retry/post_repair/post_reenter/post_block: select a higher-priority lawful action if one exists; otherwise follow the still-lawful current edge; otherwise if authority is missing reprice or block; otherwise block with typed no-action. These reprice/block outputs are selection no-actions, not evaluate_action closure decisions. Unresolved post_reprice returns no_action(undeclared), naming missing outcome/bound and declaring re-entry; reevaluation requires separately admitted exact outcome/bounded basis through new initial_selection or basis-bearing resume. Even default graph following is an explicit evaluate_next decision.

exceptions: An earlier result stands for a no-action only if it decided the same predicate on the current basis.

grounding.quote:
Where the graph is complete and no action follows a closed edge, nothing
is refused and no selection determination is made: the empty selection is
invocational data, and `close` keeps its own value for the edge predicate
under A8.

constraints.statement: Selected next invocation is invocational data, not a core-result value. Every typed no-action has its own material result for 'a published lawful action can be selected for the current gap on the exact basis', both initially and after closure decisions. no_action(undeclared)→out_of_frame when a needed action is unpublished or a relation/capability/authority undeclared; name what is missing and its owner. no_action(basis)→invalid_basis when current outcome/catalogue/policy cannot support a lawful action for the gap. Keep typed no-action beside its core value; next-action projection production establishes availability only. Preceding closure results remain evidence for selection and retain their distinct edge predicate; neither predicate receives credit from the other's value. Completed-graph empty selection is not a refusal/result determination.
constraints.uncertainty: External core-result and construction-availability definitions are not supplied; the explicit local mappings are retained.

grounding.quote:
The seven decisions of A8 stay the closed vocabulary; a
refined value names a decision and its cause and adds no decision (P5,
P6).

constraints.statement: No edge closes from raw artifact presence, worker report, process success or CLI summary. AdmittedEvidence folds into EdgeFulfillmentLedger then EdgeClosureDecision. Ledger records counts, obligation rows, materialization/liveness/admission refs and edge_converged, never selects next work. Decisions form exactly {close,yield,retry,repair,re-enter,reprice,block}; each is replay-visible with reproducible basis/reason refs and exactly one cause-refined core value for 'the edge's obligations are fulfilled on the exact basis': close→satisfied on admitted fulfilment; yield→indeterminate on lawful undecided progress/wait with deciding resume basis; retry(defeated)→falsified on admissible counterevidence while same action remains lawful; every other retry, including liveness interruption alone, is retry(undecided)→indeterminate with deciding reattempt identified; repair(implementation)→falsified on an admitted failing implementation obligation; every other repair is repair(proof)→indeterminate with repaired deciding proof identified. Both repairs retain coherent governing relation/basis/target binding and address a local defect by lawful same-edge repair. re-enter(undeclared)→out_of_frame when required upstream asset/relation change needs undeclared relation/capability/authority, naming it and owner; re-enter(basis)→invalid_basis for other unsupported-current-basis causes. reprice→out_of_frame for undeclared further-work outcome/bound, naming it, owner and requested constitutional re-entry. block(undeclared)→out_of_frame when the just-taken action leaves the edge unable to proceed for undeclared relation/capability/authority; block(basis)→invalid_basis for other unsupported-basis causes. For re-enter/block with both undeclared and basis causes, record both and use basis. Cause is read from required basis/reason refs and adds no eighth decision or new core value.

grounding.quote:
In §11.5D, §16 and §19 "disposition" names a closure decision (the
selected-outcome paragraphs, A8, A11, the constitutional equation, §16
item 13 and §19 question 11) or, in "typed no-action disposition", a
selection of `evaluate_next` (A3, A4); there it never names a disposition
of ACTIVATION §3. The dispositions of §21 are the successor dispositions
of [RELEASE §9](RELEASE.md#9-successor-baseline-conservation-stdo-up-015)
(P1, P5, P6).

constraints.statement: The bounded action's candidate-availability result, edge-obligation closure result and acceptance disposition answer distinct predicates; no value counts toward another predicate. Closure decisions must never be recorded as ACTIVATION §3 accept/local_repair/re_enter/reject, nor vice versa. In particular repair(proof)=indeterminate differs from local_repair=falsified, and re-enter(undeclared)=out_of_frame differs from re_enter=invalid_basis. In ODD §11.5D/§16/§19, disposition means closure decision, except typed no-action disposition means evaluate_next selection; §21 dispositions instead concern RELEASE §9 successor conservation.

grounding.quote:
A10 Liveness does not close semantic truth. Liveness observes activity,
inactivity, process state and interruption. It can support yield or a
liveness interruption; it cannot by itself declare semantic failure,
semantic closure or requirement non-satisfaction (P6).

constraints.statement: Yield requires a still-lawful same edge/attempt, admitted progress or waiting, replay-visible resume basis and control return without failure classification. It preserves the current edge for long-running/bounded/partially productive work and is not retry, block, timeout or local CLI waiting/looping. Liveness observes activity/inactivity/process/interruption and may support yield/interruption but cannot alone establish semantic failure, closure or requirement non-satisfaction. evaluate_action emits conceptual repair/re-enter decisions; evaluate_next selects their published graph-action realisations from admitted closure truth, never local string-based retry branches.

grounding.quote:
A13 requires that the decision be reproducible from the inputs;
A13a requires that each governing carrier or projection carry the predecessor refs
that make reproduction reachable without external joins. A broken
predecessor chain is non-replayable at the carrier level and therefore
fails A13 (P3, P4b).

constraints.statement: Every closure decision and next-action selection must be reproducible from RuntimeEventLog, execution basis, ABG event-log-backed IntentLineage, ProductAssetModel publication basis/event refs, selected outcome identity/admitted bounded-basis refs, GapPressureRow, TargetObligationBinding, ActionCatalog, admitted evidence, EdgeFulfillmentLedger, EdgeClosureDecision, NextActionBasis and visible policy refs. Failure to reproduce indicates hidden state. Every governing admitted/replay-derived carrier/projection carries causal predecessor refs: outcome/bounded basis→target binding, and lineage→model→gap→binding→priority→selected-action NextActionProjection→ConstructionIntent→evidence→ledger→decision→NextActionBasis→next NextActionProjection. The first projection admits intent preserving authority refs; the second consumes post-action basis and fresh gap truth. Both are predecessor-reachable without external joins; a broken carrier chain fails replayability.

conditions: A graph function publishes refinement of an outer vector into inner vectors.
exceptions: An intentionally opaque inner realisation remains implementation within one bounded action and may use local control flow solely to compute that action's internal result.

grounding.quote:
An intentionally opaque inner realisation is
ordinary implementation inside one bounded action: it may use local
control flow to compute the action's internal result, but it must not
publish, dispatch, retry, repair, re-enter or close graph work as a hidden
traversal controller. Once a refinement is published as graph structure,
the loop governs it recursively (P4a, P0, P6).

constraints.statement: Each published inner-vector boundary obeys all four functions with its own visible model, gap, binding, action, evidence, ledger, closure and next-action projection. Opaque implementation must not publish, dispatch, retry, repair, re-enter or close graph work as hidden traversal control. ABG retains runtime/replay/lifecycle/supervision/continuation/re-entry mechanics; product retains domain asset/catalogue meaning, gap interpretation and priority policy. The software-design profile governs modules within this split and must not fragment eval_gap/evaluate_next/evaluate_action into module-local decision authorities.
constraints.uncertainty: The referenced DESIGN_MODULE/PROFILES rules are not supplied.

conditions: A ticket, design, code module or proof touches model synthesis, the evaluation functions, traversal, gaps, selection, intent, worker invocation, evidence admission, fulfilment, liveness, closure, re-entry, public query or live proof.
exceptions: Unchanged accepted relations cite their accepted basis and are not proved again.

grounding.quote:
the causally
applicable members of this axiom set and the constitutional equation below
are the controlling acceptance constraints for the selected Product
outcome and the affected published boundary. Unchanged accepted relations
cite their accepted basis and are not proved again. The axiom family
authorises no horizontal realisation growth, creates no Product work and
does not widen the selected outcome (P6, P2).

constraints.statement: Only causally applicable axioms and equation control acceptance for the selected outcome and affected published boundary; the family creates no Product work, widens no outcome and authorises no horizontal realisation growth. Local ticket wording, test names, source-grep checks, CLI summaries and implementation notes cannot weaken it. Local completion with a rival traversal-consequence path is not constitutional completion: request lawful re-entry, retain a closure blocker, or separately admit bounded paydown under an independently selected outcome/prerequisite. Gap dossiers, postflight/assurance reports, materialization manifests, liveness projections, run summaries, worker prose, screen/PTY transcripts, prompt packages, harness target arguments, source-grep tests, CLI branches/output, public query/gaps views and service outputs provide evidence/diagnostics/read context only, never independently close/select/route retry, repair or re-entry. In conflict, admitted ledger→decision→next-projection chain prevails; if absent, constitutional closure and next selection have not occurred.

exceptions: post_reprice without separately admitted constitutional basis yields typed no-action pending re-entry.

grounding.quote:
The implementation is correct only when the next work decision is derived
from that equation, `U` stays causally reachable through the target
binding and the construction intent, and no other path can decide what
work happens next (P6, P2).

constraints.statement: The represented equation proceeds: U=(selected outcome ref, optional admitted bounded-basis ref); L=event-log projection of source/prior intent; M0=synthesize_model(L,prior model,admitted product truth); G0=eval_gap(M0,event log,runtime projection,worksite), with O=G0.observation; B0=bind(U,G0.pressures,catalogue,target obligations); Q0=initial_selection(L,M0); N0=evaluate_next(Q0,G0,B0,catalogue,policy); I=admit_construction_intent(L,B0,N0.selected_action,N0.next_action_projection); E=admit_evidence(invoke(I)); A=evaluate_action(I,E,B0,policy); M1=synthesize_model(L,M0,admitted product truth); G1=eval_gap(M1,event log,runtime projection,worksite); B1=bind(U,G1.pressures,catalogue,target obligations); Q1=next_action_basis_from(A.decision); N1=evaluate_next(Q1,G1,B1,catalogue,policy); return N1. A carries ledger and one of seven decisions; Q1 is one of seven post-action bases. Correctness requires next work derive from this equation, U remain causally reachable through binding/intent, and no alternative next-work path. This is an interpretation of source operations, not their execution.
constraints.uncertainty: The pseudocode's operational implementation and external admission definitions are not supplied.

grounding.quote:
This profile gives the product shape, not the domain semantics. The same
ODD structural law can build many different domain products, and each
product defines its own asset meanings, proof lanes and query overlays.
Structural GTL law and product-specific semantic law are never confused
(P1).

constraints.statement: ODD supplies structural shape, while each domain product defines its asset meanings, proof lanes and query overlays. Structural GTL law must remain distinct from product-specific semantic law; shared structural law supports many domain products.

grounding.quote:
Automation must stay true for a manual walkthrough. A human operator using
only the declared authority surfaces should be able to (P0, P6):

constraints.statement: Automation must preserve the manual process. Using only declared authority surfaces, a human should identify current state/typed asset or node; next lawful vector and public graph function (transition contract versus constructive program); inputs/evaluators/output contract/carried environment; construct or assess the next asset/checkpoint; and repeat to target-relative closure. Automation may improve speed/safety/repeatability and render prompts, scaffold artifacts, select steps, run workers, collect evidence and assess closure through those authorities; it cannot invent a different process, skip undeclared nodes, fabricate authority, collapse constitutional transitions opaquely without declared refinement, depend on unavailable implementation-carrier knowledge, or merge installed-builder and under-development-product authority during self-host work. Unexplainable manual traversal means automation is not yet method-safe.

grounding.quote:
A derived surface or projected frame of the general method may
orient the agent to source precedence, lawful re-entry and traceability;
it must not be used to decide product-specific behaviour, which must come
from the current product authority packet

constraints.statement: The F_P walkthrough follows real work end-to-end using declared authority only: intake triage, smallest lawful re-entry, specification→requirement→design→ticket chain, constructive evaluation loop and closure proof. The minimal packet includes declared input/output contract, required context, role, evaluator regime and provenance, containing only smallest sufficient authority with source refs; memory/wholesale hidden context is not its basis. Compression is prompt input, never deciding authority; derived general-method surfaces may orient precedence/re-entry/traceability but product-specific behaviour comes from current product authority. Work must have correct change class, traceability and admission. Tickets, change-class declarations, design derivations and execution contracts pass deterministic fail-closed admission under SPEC_METHOD/TICKETS, naming violated rules; a drafted classification is not automatic truth. Walkthrough and passed admission are conformance evidence, not ratification; repeated execution does not amend shared method or constitutionalise grey work.
constraints.uncertainty: General admission rules and ODD §9 governance are referenced but not supplied.

conditions: A walkthrough cannot proceed.

grounding.quote:
An agent that ignored the declared authority, relied on stale memory or
reasoned badly has produced agent error, not a method defect. Admission
rejects the malformed artifact either way, so a bad agent turn neither
becomes law nor silently indicts the method (P6).

constraints.statement: A blockage is a method defect only if a competent, correctly configured agent using declared authority cannot decide because the owning surface has ambiguity, missing step, contradictory authority or undecidable change class; reprice that defect into its owner. Ignoring authority, stale memory or bad reasoning is agent error. Admission rejects malformed artifacts either way. Walkthrough proof is independent of automated-runtime availability: overloaded APIs/flaky transport cannot establish constitutional process soundness because they conflate process validity with execution availability.

conditions: Negative proof for an ODD or graph-native boundary.
exceptions: The detailed supported identity chain applies where those identities apply.

grounding.quote:
Closure-grade negative evidence identifies the supported entry and the
governing authority; invalidates the real authority-bearing input;
exercises the supported path; proves refusal before the prohibited
effect; and establishes that no legacy, fallback, reconstruction or
parallel path succeeds. Source, packaged, installed and runtime absence
are distinct claims (P6, P3).

constraints.statement: Exercise the supported Product authority path, never manufacture the refusal/event/gap/verdict to be derived. Closure-grade evidence identifies entry/authority, invalidates real authority-bearing input, exercises that path, proves refusal before prohibited effect and excludes successful legacy/fallback/reconstruction/parallel paths. Keep source, packaged, installed and runtime absence distinct. Where applicable the chain is public entry→admitted GTL composition owning topology→named GraphFunction callable contract→implementation/plugin only at admitted seam→ABG traversal/event/continuation/replay truth→replay-derived projection→typed Product outcome/continuation. CLI, SDK, service, adapter, plugin, fixture, query and projection cannot become rival controllers. Consumer owns concrete test/evidence mechanism; this section owns the required property.

grounding.quote:
Each retained `GraphFunction` should declare `environment.requires`,
`environment.provides` and `environment.carries`. A later function may
require any typed binding available in the cumulative carried
environment, not only the immediately previous output (P4a, P4b).

A product that publishes graph functions without this cumulative
environment law has a line that is graph-shaped but structurally wrong

constraints.statement: Composition uses a mandatory cumulative typed environment, not merely last-output-to-next-input wiring. Each retained GraphFunction should declare environment.requires/provides/carries. Later functions may require any available cumulatively carried typed binding. Publishing graph functions without this law is structurally wrong despite graph shape; the field-declaration recommendation remains 'should'.

conditions: An outer public carrier is refined into executable inner structure, or current Product closure is claimed.
exceptions: A live requirement without a witness ceases to hold the carrier open when realised, explicitly deferred, or explicitly repriced out of the active branch.

grounding.quote:
For current product closure, live current requirements that lack an
executable proof witness keep the enclosing carrier open until they are
realised, explicitly deferred, or explicitly repriced out of the active
branch. For the active software line the immediate pressure is usually a
realised testcase or archived test evidence, but the governing law is
proof-lane aware: the witness must be a governed realised proof surface
appropriate to the requirement class (P2, P6).

constraints.statement: Local green arcs are insufficient: inner chains close lawfully, coarse enclosing contract remains true after fold-back, and zoomed/unzoomed views agree on enclosing open/closed state. Live current requirements without executable proof keep the enclosing carrier open under the stated exceptions. Witnesses must be governed realised proof surfaces appropriate to requirement class; realised testcase/archived test evidence is usually the software-line pressure, not a universal proof format.

grounding.quote:
The best proving paths come from declared scenarios and use cases,
because they pressure both feature intent and design decisions. That makes
them the best source for selecting the significant code and control paths
the system must exercise (P2).

constraints.statement: Scenario bundles should expose feature/use-case boundary, expected starting assets, expected vectors, significant exercised paths and closing evidence. Declared scenarios/use cases are the preferred proving-path source for significant code/control paths the system must exercise; the bundle's 'should' is not strengthened to 'must'.

conditions: The product has an installable development form.

grounding.quote:
Where the product has an installable development form, decisive proof
runs against that installed development form in an isolated environment.
For a graph-native ODD product the proving lane should exercise install,
project bootstrap, graph traversal, evidence collection and
target-relative closure. Direct source checks stay useful and do not
replace installed-dev proof (P6, P3). This rule is the profile's binding of
[ASSURANCE §5 Installed dev proof](ASSURANCE.md#5-installed-dev-proof), which
owns it.

constraints.statement: Decisive proof runs against the installed development form in isolation. A graph-native ODD proving lane should exercise install, bootstrap, traversal, evidence collection and target-relative closure. Direct source checks remain useful but cannot replace installed proof. ASSURANCE §5 owns the imported rule.

grounding.quote:
The product should be developed through the same graph-native method it
claims to provide. Where the product provides ODD framework behaviour, it
must build that behaviour through ODD graph functions and must not merely
publish ODD-shaped artifacts after imperative execution has already
decided the work. The project should therefore increasingly describe and
build itself through explicit assets, explicit vectors, explicit graph
functions, explicit scenario bundles and explicit target-relative closure.
The method is stronger when the product can walk itself (P0, P6).

constraints.statement: The product should use its own claimed graph-native method and increasingly describe/build itself with explicit assets, vectors, graph functions, scenarios and target-relative closure. Where it provides ODD framework behaviour, building that behaviour through ODD graph functions is mandatory; imperative work selection followed only by ODD-shaped publication is prohibited.

grounding.quote:
A release version is not constitutional graph truth; it belongs to the
release process and release metadata. The graph-native method concerns
current assets, current vectors, current closures and current authority.
Immutable RC publication, version-line selector advancement and exact-cut
acceptance stay a separate process surface, [RELEASE](RELEASE.md) (P3,
P6).

constraints.statement: Release version belongs to release process/metadata, not constitutional graph truth about current assets, vectors, closures and authority. Immutable RC publication, version-line selector advancement and exact-cut acceptance remain the separate RELEASE surface.
constraints.uncertainty: RELEASE's detailed process is not supplied.

conditions: Any enumerated failure pattern holds.

grounding.quote: This profile is violated when any of these holds (P6):

constraints.statement: Each is independently a profile violation: claimed step without node/vector; function without clear outer contract; automation inexplicable as manual traversal; installed dependence on authoring knowledge absent from a clean target; scenarios unable to name significant proving paths; closure without target-relative evidence; last-output wiring bypassing cumulative environment; inconsistent zoom closure; imperative service transition without published outcome contract; orchestration-first framework later labelled GTL; imperative closure/continuation/semantic movement/lineage outside declared graph-function, ABG or product carrier truth; hidden product/plugin execution authority over traversal, invocation, supervision, retry, continuation, events, projection or closure; flattening yield into retry/block/timeout/local wait/hidden CLI loop; query/gaps/postflight/service/operator summaries deciding work outside the loop; or constitutional process not followable end-to-end from declared authority, or artifact accepted without deterministic admission.
constraints.uncertainty: The detailed method-defect versus agent-error conditions remain those of §11.7A.

conditions: An agent/designer is told 'using ODD, build this product'.
exceptions: Read a product-specific method only if one exists.

grounding.quote:
14. only then implement code, policy and transport surfaces.

The instruction does not mean starting from imperative scripts and adding
GTL words later, treating graph functions as documentation wrappers, or
letting service code become the hidden real carrier (P0, P6).

constraints.statement: Expected order: read SPEC_METHOD and preserve constitutional chain; read existing product-specific method; read local INTENT.md, PRODUCT.md, requirements and active designs; identify source→published-outcome semantic chain; identify typed domain assets/nodes; identify public graph functions; define machine-readable catalogue; define/update GTL outer carriers and traversal boundaries; define scale-consistent coarse/refined/proof closure; complete audit for affected execution surfaces; define intent/model→observation→binding→selection→admitted evidence→ledger→closure→next-projection loop; define closed decision vocabulary including lawful yield; define admitted-history query/projection lane and structural coherence; only then implement code/policy/transport. Imperative-first GTL labelling, documentation-wrapper graph functions and hidden service carriers are excluded.
constraints.uncertainty: This records an expected subject workflow, not an instruction executed here.

conditions: Starting cold in a concrete ODD product.

grounding.quote: Starting cold in a concrete ODD product, read in the order below (P1, P2).

In practice this profile sets the structural expectation, the
product-specific method sets the domain law, and the local product
surfaces set the current build line. An LLM that skips the order will
usually either understand the paradigm but miss the domain, or understand
the domain but realise it through the wrong carrier (P1, P2).

constraints.statement: General order: SPEC_METHOD→ODD profile→stdo_<label>.json→applicable bound reference-frame basis and authorised activation packet→bound product Intent→bound Product definition→relevant bound requirements→active bound designs→GTL module/catalogue/query surfaces. World-model order inserts WORLD_MODEL after ODD, uses relevant requirement families/current designs, and includes proof lane in the final step. ODD sets structure, product-specific method domain law, and local surfaces current build line. Skipping usually causes paradigm/domain or domain/carrier mismatch; 'usually' is not certainty.
constraints.uncertainty: Reading targets not embedded here remain unresolved, unvisited references.

conditions: An LLM is ramping into an ODD product.

grounding.quote:
If those questions cannot be answered quickly, the product is not yet
sufficiently ODD-shaped (P0, P2).

constraints.statement: The LLM should quickly answer all fourteen: semantic chain; typed assets/nodes; public graph functions; catalogue location; GTL location; ABG/product split; query lane; each projection's admitted source and structural-drift refusal; evidence execution authority has not escaped ABG; observation-to-next-action loop; closure decisions and replay-visible yield; proof surfaces closing capabilities; outer carrier remaining open despite green inner lane when requirements lack proof; and whether declared-authority-only agentic process is followable with deterministic artifact admission. Inability to answer quickly means not yet sufficiently ODD-shaped, not a performed completeness judgment here.

grounding.quote: Seven clauses have no predecessor row and are new.
